study_identification.author_journal_year: Floris et al., Nature Mental Health, 2025
study_identification.title: A multimodal neural signature of face processing in autism within the fusiform gyrus

study_characteristics.study_objective: To investigate the multimodal neural signature of face processing in autism within the fusiform gyrus (FFG) by integrating data from structural MRI, resting-state fMRI, task-fMRI, and EEG. The study aimed to identify how individual-level deviations across these modalities differentiate autistic from non-autistic individuals and relate to social functioning in autism.

imaging_modality.answer: structural MRI; resting-state fMRI; task-fMRI; EEG

preprocessing_pipeline.answer: CAT12; SPM12; FSL; ICA-AROMA; EEGLab; Fieldtrip

quality_checking_detail.answer: sMRI: Excluded based on weighted overall image quality ratings from CAT12. rs-fMRI: Excluded for excessive head motion (meanFD > 0.7mm or maxFD > 7.6mm), fewer than 180 volumes, or extreme values. task-fMRI: Excluded for excessive head motion (>20% of trials with meanFD > 0.5mm). EEG: Excluded for too few trials (<20) or channels (<75%).

site_effect_handling_detail.answer: Scanning site was included as a covariate in the Bayesian Linear Regression normative models.

response_variable.answer: sMRI: Voxel-wise GM volumes; rs-fMRI: Seed-based connectivity from FFA; task-fMRI: T-contrast maps (faces vs shapes); EEG: Principal component of source-reconstructed activation.

predictor_effects.answer: Age, Sex, and Site were modeled as covariates (fixed effects).

nm_vldtn_handle_ns.reason: The model explicitly includes age, sex, and scanning site as covariates to account for these nuisance variables.
nm_vldtn_handle_ns.supporting_text: Here, we trained normative models using Bayesian linear regression 98 for each brain imaging modality within the right and left FFG region of interest (ROI) independently using age, sex and scanning site as covariates.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.reason: The model performance was evaluated using metrics like Rho, EV, and MSLL, which are calculated on the training data.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.supporting_text: The accuracy of the normative model was evaluated using the correlation between the recorded and the predicted voxel values (Rho), mean standardized log loss, standardized mean squared error and the EV (Supplementary Fig. 1) as well as based on the forward models (Extended Data Fig. 1).

nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.reason: The use of 10-fold cross-validation ensures that the model is tested on data that was not used for training in each fold.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.supporting_text: Normative models were derived in an unbiased manner across the entire sample under tenfold cross-validation.

nm_vldtn_diff_domain.reason: The paper does not mention any validation of the normative model on an external or different domain dataset.

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Canonical Correlation Analysis (CCA) was used to model the multivariate relationship between the multimodal independent components (derived from Z-deviations) and social-communicative features.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Multimodal neural signatures within the fusiform gyrus differentiate autistic from non-autistic individuals and are specifically associated with social, but not non-social, functioning in autism.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: A significant group difference was found in a multimodal component (IC44), driven by functional modalities (rs-fMRI, EEG) and structure, in both face-selective and retinotopic areas of the FFG. Multimodal components outperformed unimodal ones in classifying individuals (AUC 0.64 vs 0.48). Furthermore, a CCA revealed a significant association between a set of multimodal ICs and social-communicative features (r=0.65), but not non-social features, with ADOS social affect, RMET, and face-matching performance being the largest behavioral contributors.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: The analysis was restricted to the FFG, not the whole brain. The sample size for a four-modality analysis was relatively small, precluding sex-stratified analyses. The number of left-handed individuals was too small to analyze handedness effects. Variability in task paradigms for face processing localization is a general issue.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: The study combined normative modeling to get individual deviation maps (Z-scores) per modality and then used Linked Independent Component Analysis (LICA) to fuse these maps and identify multimodal signatures of inter-subject variability.

general_notes.general_notes: The study used imputed clinical data to handle missing values and maximize sample size. The authors highlight that the superiority of multimodal approaches depends on the presence of biologically meaningful, shared information across modalities.
